root_motivation: **Who:** every Rust branch in the build loop, and the operator who reads `blockers=hermetic-build` as "the build phoned home".
user_persona: The autobuilder skill orchestrator (a Claude session) and the human invoking `/autobuilder` from their own project. Both shell out to this binary for the receipt + gate steps that must not live in bash.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a fake `cargo` that dumps its env, When hermetic-build runs under a parent env with `BUILD_BURST_ENABLED=1 BURST_LANE=1`, Then the dump shows `BUILD_BURST_ENABLED=0` and `BURST_LANE=0` and no `BURST_LANE_SH`, and the receipt has `cargo_route: "local-pinned"`.
Given a fake `cargo` that opens a TCP connection to the host's non-loopback address, When the producer runs, Then the verdict is `block`, the socket is attributed, and `route_observed` is `local`.

Given a fake `cargo` that appends `<ts> burst cargo build` to `target/autobuilder/route.log`, When the producer runs, Then the verdict is `block` with `cause: "route-not-local"` and the journal line ends `route=burst`.
Given a quiet fake `cargo` and no route.log, When the producer runs, Then the verdict is `pass`, `route_observed` is `unknown`, and `ignore_rules` is unchanged.
Given the existing `hermetic_scope_ac1..ac4` tests, When `cargo test -p extended-gates` runs, Then they still pass unchanged.

Given RedBaron with build-skill's real shim first on PATH and `BUILD_BURST_ENABLED=1`, When the producer runs on a one-file crate, Then the receipt shows `route_observed: "local"`, verdict `pass`, and the changelog quotes the receipt.

Given the shipped producer and routing re-enabled through `burst-lane.sh enable`, When the next mcphost branch gate runs, Then its blockers list does not contain `hermetic-build`; the changelog quotes the gate line.

scope: Stage 4 risk gate (7 receipts + release receipt)
non_goals: Spawning Claude subagents from the binary itself (that is the orchestrator's job)
Web-service, WASM, or embedded scaffolding (v1 supports cli + lib only)
Auto-applying self-evolution proposals (always gated for user review)
Re-running the underlying audit/test commands inside `gate` (gate only attests; producers own the work)

five_whys_trace.q: Why a Rust companion binary instead of a pure-skill scaffold?
five_whys_trace.a: Shell is too easy to subvert (set -e off, grep eaten, jq missing). The load-bearing parts — metric extraction, digest binding, schema validation — need a typed implementation under tests.

five_whys_trace.q: Why a 7-receipt gate instead of `cargo test && cargo clippy`?
five_whys_trace.a: Each receipt covers a class of failure that the others miss: clippy doesn't see CI status, tests don't see proof-lane routing, and none of them produce an independent-review record. The gate is what makes 'ready' falsifiable.

five_whys_trace.q: Why bootstrap autobuilder against itself before running it on other projects?
five_whys_trace.a: If the gate model can't certify the binary that produces gate receipts, it can't be trusted on any other project. The meta-bootstrap is the cheapest adversarial test of the whole pipeline.

five_whys_trace.q: Why deny unwrap/expect everywhere in src/ when most of this is glue code?
five_whys_trace.a: Glue code that panics on a missing receipt or malformed JSON destroys the audit trail at exactly the moments the gate matters most. Erroring back to the caller keeps the diagnostic surface alive.

five_whys_trace.q: Why digest-bind every receipt instead of trusting file timestamps?
five_whys_trace.a: Timestamps lie under git checkout. A self-binding sha256 lets the gate detect tampering and lets reviewers re-verify by recomputing on the receipt's own contents.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Where does the autobuilder repo's 'project' live for the gate — repo root or autobuilder/ workspace?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Repo root. agent/, scripts/, target/autobuilder/ all sit at /home/jsy/projects/autobuilder/. Proof-lanes globs use autobuilder/src/** prefix to match `git diff` output.
